mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises >0.5% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 y/y growth <2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-mo MA for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening in the face of rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-mo averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% m/m for two consecutive months) signals improved consumer purchasing power, which boosts demand and supports higher corporate earnings, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows >0.5% m/m for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% while payroll growth (PAYEMS) accelerates above its 12-month average indicates an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and may prompt restrictive monetary policy, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with wage inflation risk
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 12-mo average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related economic activity and consumer confidence, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-mo MA for four months.
